title: How Hackers Crack Passwords (and How to Stop Them) 🔐 #shorts
description:
Good websites never store your actual password, so how do hackers still crack it? They steal password hashes in a breach, then make billions of guesses per second, starting with leaked password lists and common words, hashing each guess and looking for a match. Length is your best protection, salts and slow hashes make guessing expensive, and a password manager plus two-factor authentication keeps you safe.

lines: Good websites never store your actual password. So how do hackers still crack it?
Sites store a hash: a one-way scramble. password123 always becomes the same jumble, but it can't be reversed.
When a site is breached, attackers steal those hashes. Then they guess, billions of times per second, hashing each guess, looking for a match.
They start with leaked password lists and common words, like sunshine, qwerty, or your pet's name with a 1 on the end.
Length is what saves you. A random 8 character password can fall in hours. At 16, it could outlast the universe.
So use long, unique passwords from a password manager, and turn on two-factor authentication.
Hash. Guess. Compare. Now you know what you're up against.
